correctness.rationale: For the side-two cube and Haar central-plane law, convolution of three uniform coordinates gives the exact area formula in each of the four- and six-vertex chambers. Independent cube-edge hull calculations agree for 540 directions. Ball extremizers restrict the upper-tail event to finitely many corners. Uniform first-order two-chamber deficit expansions bound the rescaled event; dominated convergence gives domain areas 1/16 and (2+pi)/32. The spherical Jacobian and 12/pi multiplicity give the exact two joint-tail coefficients. Finite-threshold numerical quadrature approaches both limits but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The cube maximizes central-section area exactly on the interface between quadrilateral and hexagonal combinatorics. A non-smooth, piecewise homogeneous local deficit makes the extreme-area probability a distinct natural invariant. Exact four/ six-chamber tail coefficients show that a majority of almost-maximal sections are hexagonal even though the maximizers are four-sided. This materially refines classical max-section and random-face-count results without claiming a general all-dimensional theory.
